why: Fixture envelope must be signed before enrollment/service exists; constructing a fake minimal service would be circular. The genuinely observed held fixture key can expose a restricted source-owned envelope signer before actual service adoption.
semantics: Registry retains genuine held key observation/current source-root/controller lease. Signer checks actual registry membership, exact v164 closed publication fields/current namespace/key/source/controller and hashes before signing exactly v164 canonical envelope preimage at hermes-installer.qualification-enrollment.v1. No arbitrary bytes/domain, caller key, fake minimal AuthorityService, production key copy or other-purpose signing. Returned string uses the existing authority signature codec; envelope.signature holds it. Verify performs same current key/source/namespace checks, not caller bool proof. Publisher retains signer capability internally and must reopen/recheck authority/catalog/generation bytes before signing; hash syntax alone never establishes provenance.
adoption: After verified publication, AuthorityService.from_root_qualification adopts the SAME actual key observation/custody capability via restricted fixture runtime registry. No second key or new trust root. Source-owned signer facade reuses existing authority signature primitive/domain handling without requiring an already instantiated service. Supersedes v162 wording requiring actual service before envelope publication.

tasks.work: Implement restricted prepublication envelope signer and postpublication same-key AuthorityService adoption; reject unrelated fields/domains/namespace, expired key/source lease and arbitrary hash claims.

acceptance: No operational acceptance implied; all AC open; baseline unchanged.
